S2_cache_keys_branch_scoped.scenario: Cache keys all branch-scoped (no global 'menu' without branch suffix)
S2_cache_keys_branch_scoped.v2_classification: V2-BLOCKER for 2 keys / V1-OK-V2-WATCH for 1 key / V2-OK for all business cache
evidence_branch_keyed_safe: Cash drawer & delivery boy locks (CashDrawerService.php:78, DeliveryBoyCashSessionService.php:82) — branch + user keyed, V2-OK
Order idempotency Cache::lock per (branch, user, hash) (OrderService.php:627, FrontendOrderService.php:157) — V2-OK
evidence_global_keys_problematic: 'outbox.retry-failed.lock' (OutboxRetryFailedCommand.php:42 LOCK_KEY = literal constant) — V2-BLOCKER. One slow branch retry serially blocks ALL branches' outbox retries.
'outbox.webhook-retry-failed.lock' (OutboxWebhookRetryFailedCommand.php:62 LOCK_KEY = literal constant) — V2-BLOCKER. Same as above for webhook retries.

'ws:heartbeat' (DispatchDomainEventsJob.php:129 + SyncOverviewController.php:531) — V1-OK-V2-WATCH. Used for cross-worker WS-up observability. V2 multi-resto wants per-branch dashboards: should become 'ws:heartbeat:branch:{id}'.
S2_cache_keys_branch_scoped.v2_impact: Two outbox retry cron commands hold a GLOBAL Cache::lock for the WHOLE retry batch. In V2 with 50 branches × concurrent retries, branch_id=37's slow Pusher endpoint will starve branch_id=12's retry until lock TTL expires. Sequential not parallel. Per-branch retry sharding required.
S2_cache_keys_branch_scoped.remediation_proposal: V2 prerequisite — extend OutboxRetryFailedCommand + OutboxWebhookRetryFailedCommand to accept --branch=N flag + per-branch Cache::lock('outbox.retry-failed.branch.{n}'). Cron schedule expands to one entry per branch (or job dispatch fan-out). 'ws:heartbeat' key add branch suffix at same time.

S3_echo_channels_branch_scoped.evidence: C6-multi-tab-echo.json C6-ARCH-001 confirms single unified 'private-branch.{branchId}' channel with per-event-name filtering. routes/channels.php:41-62 authz callback enforces branch_id isolation at subscription layer: kiosk-token → own machine's branch only; Admin/Tenant Admin → cross-branch allowed (V1 single-tenant pattern, V2 wants more granular); regular staff → own branch_id only.
S3_echo_channels_branch_scoped.v2_impact: Channel architecture is V2-ready. V2 multi-tenant addition needed: routes/channels.php:56-58 'Admin' role currently allows CROSS-BRANCH subscribe — V2 needs tenant_admin scope (one restaurant's admin cannot subscribe to another restaurant's channel). Minor authz callback patch, not a refactor.
S3_echo_channels_branch_scoped.remediation_proposal: V2.0 — tighten routes/channels.php Admin authz branch to scope by tenant_id (one tenant_admin can subscribe to all of HIS tenant's branches, not Le Cayenne's). Single-file ~10 LOC change. CITES C6-ARCH-001.

S4_storage_paths_branch_scoped.scenario: Storage paths branch-scoped (or designed for it)
evidence: config/media-library.php:7 → MEDIA_DISK=env('public') — single disk, no branch prefix
config/media-library.php:66 → Spatie DefaultPathGenerator stores at storage/app/public/{media_id}/filename (media_id is globally unique auto-increment, no branch in path)
Firebase JSON moved to 'firebase_private' disk by goal-heal-sec-001 (storage/app/firebase/...) — separate disk for sensitive secrets, but still global not per-branch
S4_storage_paths_branch_scoped.v2_impact: V1 single-tenant SAFE — media_id is globally unique, no collision risk. V2 multi-resto: (a) per-tenant CDN routing impossible (all media on one disk), (b) per-tenant backup extraction impossible (cannot 'dump just tenant X's photos'), (c) tenant offboarding requires DB scan of media table by branch FK chain (slow). Not a P0 V2 BLOCKER but a V2 architectural friction point.
S4_storage_paths_branch_scoped.remediation_proposal: V2 design — switch path_generator to a custom BranchAwarePathGenerator that returns 'branch/{branch_id}/{media_id}/{filename}'. Requires Spatie path generator override + migration to re-shuffle existing media files (storage migration script). Defer to V2.0.

S5_backup_script_multi_resto.scenario: Backup script multi-resto-friendly (Q14 backup script — scan)
evidence: scripts/backup-foodking-daily.sh:55-61 → mysqldump --single-transaction dumps ENTIRE DB foodking — multi-tenant safe (all branches share schema, all rows captured) but indivisible (cannot extract 'just tenant 37')
app/Console/Commands/Backup/RunDailyBackup.php (Q14 Laravel command) → same whole-DB dump pattern, 3-tier retention (30d daily + 12mo monthly + 24q quarterly = 6yr NF525)
scripts/db/backup.sh + scripts/restore-foodking-from-backup.sh → whole-DB restore (drops + recreates entire schema)
S5_backup_script_multi_resto.v2_impact: V1 single-tenant Le Cayenne: backup design is excellent (NF525-compliant, atomic, retention OK). V2 multi-resto: (a) tenant offboarding REQUIRES 'dump just tenant X' for GDPR portability — current backup cannot do this, (b) restore drill for one tenant impossible without affecting all, (c) backup file grows linearly with tenant count (50 tenants × 6yr retention = quarterly file size × 50 → S3 cost grows linearly).
S5_backup_script_multi_resto.remediation_proposal: V2 design — add a 'tenant_extract' sub-command that filters mysqldump by branch_id (via --where clauses on every multi-tenant table). Trickier than expected because audit_logs.branch_id is NULLABLE (B3.3 AMBER-F11) — system-level rows need explicit handling. Alternative: per-tenant DB schema (microservice-style). Defer V2.0.

S9_loyalty_cards_branch_or_cross_branch.scenario: Loyalty cards branch-scoped or cross-branch by design choice
evidence: app/Models/LoyaltyTransaction.php — no BranchScope import; keyed by user_id + loyalty_code (cross-branch by design)
database/migrations/2026_05_19_100000_create_loyalty_qr_nonces_consumed_table.php:60-63 — explicit comment: 'GLOBAL unique on nonce (per advisor — customer scans at any branch, no branch_id scoping)'
Customer model in EXEMPTED_MODELS (B3.3 DBA-F4) — architectural exemption due to Sanctum customer-token recursion risk
FrontendOrder.loyalty_customer_code, Order.loyalty_customer_code, LoyaltyService::refundPoints — all operate by loyalty_code, not branch_id
S9_loyalty_cards_branch_or_cross_branch.v2_impact: V1 single-tenant: trivially OK. V2 multi-resto: this is a business model decision — does a customer's loyalty card work at ALL of Tenant Lecayenne's branches OR across all restaurants on the SaaS platform? Currently the schema is platform-wide (any user, any branch). For V2 SaaS, the loyalty_code likely needs tenant_id scoping: 'this loyalty card is valid for Tenant X's branches only'.
S9_loyalty_cards_branch_or_cross_branch.remediation_proposal: V2.0 product decision — owner choice: (a) keep platform-wide (cross-tenant loyalty network, FoodKing-branded), or (b) scope to tenant_id (each restaurant chain owns its own loyalty). Both are valid V2 product strategies. Schema change required for option (b): add tenant_id to LoyaltyTransaction + loyalty_qr_nonces_consumed.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: smartisan/settings — ALL 31 call sites use GLOBAL group, none use the nullableMorphs('settingable') column

evidence.all_callsites_use_global: grep 'Settings::group' app/ returns 31 distinct call sites — every single one calls Settings::group('site|notification|order_setup|loyalty|pos|...')->get(...) with NO settingable parameter (global per-tenant value)
affected_features: loyalty point rates pointsPerEuro, pointsFor1Euro, minRedeem, rawTiers (Settings::group('loyalty'))
OTP / SMS / order_setup / Stripe currency config — all settings:group GLOBAL

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: smartisan/settings supports per-model settings via settingable morph. The migration includes it. The codebase does not. V2 multi-resto needs per-tenant currency, per-tenant pos_dine_in_enabled, per-tenant loyalty rates, per-tenant FCM project — none of these can vary by tenant in current code. Highest-blast-radius V2 refactor: all 31 call sites need re-routing to a tenant-scoped Settings reader (e.g. SettingsForTenant::group('site')->get(...)).
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: Without this refactor, V2 launching a second tenant means ALL of Tenant B's restaurants share Tenant A's currency / loyalty rules / FCM topic / dine-in flag. Show-stopper for V2 SaaS.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2.0 prerequisite — create SettingsForTenant facade that resolves Tenant from request context, then queries settings where settingable_type='Tenant' AND settingable_id=$tenantId. Migrate 31 call sites. Add sentinel test 'no Settings::group() call without tenant scope' that ratchets the count down. ~2 weeks of work.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: OutboxRetryFailedCommand + OutboxWebhookRetryFailedCommand hold GLOBAL Cache::lock — serializes retries across all branches

evidence.file_a: app/Console/Commands/OutboxRetryFailedCommand.php:42 — private const LOCK_KEY = 'outbox.retry-failed.lock'; (literal constant string, not branch-keyed)
evidence.ttl: LOCK_TTL_SECONDS = 300 in both — 5-minute single-tenant lock window
evidence.schedule: Kernel.php cron schedules these as periodic jobs; comment on OutboxRetryFailedCommand.php:28 says 'TTL raised 60→300s (Wave 3c) because audit-chain Cache::lock'

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: V1 single-branch: lock+process+release fine. V2 50 branches × shared lock means one branch's slow Pusher dispatch blocks ALL branches' retry attempts for up to 5 minutes. Order-status broadcasts to KDS/POS/OSS will stall during the lock window. Real-time SLA breaks under load.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: Cross-tenant contention on shared cron lock. Tenant A's outbox backlog blocks Tenant B's broadcasts. Cascade failure mode at scale.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2 prerequisite — extend signature to accept --branch=N flag; replace LOCK_KEY constant with 'outbox.retry-failed.branch.{n}'. Cron schedule: fan out one entry per branch (Kernel.php → foreach branch). Alternative: dispatch a Job-per-branch and let queue parallelism handle it. ~1 day of work + 1 day of cron operational testing.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: Queues 'high' + 'notifications' shared across all branches — no per-branch queue routing

evidence.file_c: config/queue.php — no per-branch queue connection infrastructure (single 'redis' / 'database' connection)

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: Laravel onQueue('name') is a runtime string. V2 can introduce per-tenant queues like 'high.tenant.{id}' OR per-branch 'high.branch.{id}' WITHOUT touching the calling code if the Job's queue resolution becomes config-driven. The infrastructure isn't there yet, but it's a routing layer not a rewrite.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: V1 single-tenant: no issue. V2 multi-tenant: one tenant's traffic burst can starve another tenant's high-priority broadcasts (queue worker reads any 'high' job FIFO). Mitigable with per-tenant Redis priorities + dedicated queue workers per tenant tier.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2 design — runtime-configurable queue name per Job via app(QueueRouter::class)->routeFor($job). Introduce per-tenant queue workers (supervisor config). Mitigable post-launch, NOT a V1 blocker. Defer V2.0.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: 'ws:heartbeat' Cache key is GLOBAL — V2 wants per-branch heartbeat dashboard
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: Single observability key tells admin 'is WS up'. V1 single-tenant: fine. V2 multi-tenant: admin wants 'is WS up for tenant X branch 7?' — need 'ws:heartbeat:branch:{id}' or 'ws:heartbeat:tenant:{id}'. Trivial 2-line patch when V2 happens.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: Observability gap — one branch's WS outage can be masked by another branch's still-fresh heartbeat key.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2 prerequisite (low cost) — change key to 'ws:heartbeat:branch:{id}', update SyncOverviewController to query per-branch. ~30 min of work.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: routes/channels.php Admin role allows CROSS-BRANCH Echo subscription — V2 needs tenant_admin scope
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.evidence: C6-multi-tab-echo.json V6.2 channel_inventory_actual.private-branch.{branchId}.authorization_callback_summary line 64 — 'Admin / Tenant Admin role → cross-branch allowed (V1 single-tenant pattern)'.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: V1: Admin sees all of Le Cayenne (single tenant). V2: a Tenant_Admin should ONLY see his own tenant's branches (not Tenant B's). Currently the Admin role bypass is unbounded.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: Tenant_admin cross-tenant Echo subscription = info disclosure across SaaS tenants. SECURITY-V2-BLOCKER if not heavily caveated.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2.0 — patch routes/channels.php:56-58 to scope by Tenant model relationship. ~10 LOC patch. CITES C6-ARCH-001.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: Spatie media files stored at storage/app/public/{media_id}/filename — no branch_id in path
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.evidence: config/media-library.php:66 — DefaultPathGenerator. media_id is globally unique auto-increment. Files pooled under MEDIA_DISK='public' default.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: media_id uniqueness avoids V1 collisions. V2 friction: per-tenant CDN routing impossible; tenant offboarding requires DB scan of media → branch relationship to identify the right files to extract.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: Tenant GDPR portability friction; per-tenant backup extraction friction; per-tenant CDN routing friction.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2 design — custom BranchAwarePathGenerator extending Spatie's, returning 'branch/{branch_id}/{media_id}/{filename}'. Requires data migration of existing files. Defer V2.0.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: Whole-DB backup is multi-branch-safe but NOT tenant-extractable for V2 SaaS offboarding
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.evidence: scripts/backup-foodking-daily.sh:55-61 + app/Console/Commands/Backup/RunDailyBackup.php — mysqldump --single-transaction on full DB. NF525-compliant retention (30d daily + 12mo + 24q quarterly = 6yr).
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: V1: backup design is excellent for single tenant. V2: cannot extract just one tenant's data for GDPR portability or offboarding without writing per-table --where='branch_id IN (...)' clauses. audit_logs.branch_id NULLABLE (B3.3 AMBER-F11) complicates this further.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: V2 SaaS GDPR portability impossible without backup rework. NF525 compliance preserved (whole-DB still captured), but tenant exit becomes a complex DBA task.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.remediation_proposal: V2 prerequisite — add foodking:backup-tenant {tenant_id} command that does selective dump. Handle NULL branch_id audit rows via 'system-level' bucket exposed to all tenants. CITES B3.3 AMBER-F11.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: FCM uses token-based delivery (not topic broadcast) — no per-branch topic-naming concern
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.evidence: app/Services/FirebaseService.php:17-67 — sendNotification($data, $fcmTokens, $topicName) iterates fcmTokens and POSTs per-token (line 31 'foreach ($fcmTokens as $fcmToken)'). The $topicName parameter is used as a STRING TAG in the payload['data']['topicName'] but does NOT route via /topics/X. Delivery is per-device-token, scoped by which tokens are passed in.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: Per-token delivery means each branch's customer/staff tokens are passed explicitly — no FCM-topic-namespace collision risk in V2. Tokens are scoped by branch via the caller passing only branch-relevant tokens.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: V2-OK — caller-driven scoping. As long as the upstream layer (notification dispatcher) filters tokens by branch, FCM delivery stays scoped.

additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.title: All 12 outbox listeners hard-code 'private-branch.{branch_id}' channel — V2-safe
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.evidence: grep 'private-branch' app/Listeners/Persist*.php → 12 listeners (PersistCatalogChangedToOutbox, PersistBranchStatusChangedToOutbox, PersistCouponChangedToOutbox, PersistItemVariationAvailabilityChangedToOutbox, PersistItemAvailabilityChangedToOutbox×2 (single+multi-branch), PersistItemExtraAvailabilityChangedToOutbox, PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox, PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox, PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox, PersistOrderPaidAtCounterToOutbox, PersistSettingsUpdatedToOutbox, PersistOrderTableChangedToOutbox).
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.rationale: Every Persist*ToOutbox listener composes 'private-branch.' . $branch_id dynamically. PersistItemAvailabilityChangedToOutbox even handles multi-branch via map() (line 46). The outbox channel keying is V2-ready.
additional_v2_findings_outside_10_scenar.v2_impact: V2-READY — outbox channel keying scales to N branches without code change. CITES B3.1-architect-findings.json B3-ARCH-007 (outbox pattern consistency).

verdict_summary: All 10 scoped scenarios verified. Zero V1 blockers (severity=INFO across the board per spec). TWO V2-BLOCKERS surfaced: (1) smartisan/settings global for currency/loyalty/pos/FCM/order_setup (31 call sites, highest blast radius — show-stopper for V2 multi-tenant launch), (2) outbox retry locks GLOBAL (cross-branch starvation under load). SEVEN V2-WATCH items (queues, ws:heartbeat, Echo Admin authz, Spatie media path, backup per-tenant extraction, admin report UI, loyalty cross-branch product decision) — all mitigable. THREE V2-OK items confirmed (Echo channel, fiscal sequence, outbox listeners). Sibling artifacts B3.1 + B3.3 + C6 properly cited (10 EXEMPTED_MODELS, audit_logs.branch_id NULLABLE, single private-branch channel). NF525 chain READ_ONLY_ATTESTED_NO_WRITES (no writes performed). Frozen-zones diff = 0. V1 single-tenant Le Cayenne LOCAL is SAFE; V2 SaaS requires ~2 weeks of Settings migration + ~1 day outbox lock fix + ~1 week of reports UI work + per-tenant backup tooling.

top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.title: smartisan/settings global for ALL configuration (currency, loyalty rates, pos_dine_in, FCM project, order_setup)
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.impact: 31 call sites must be re-routed to tenant-scoped Settings. Without this, V2 launching Tenant B means Tenant B's restaurants share Tenant A's currency, loyalty rules, FCM, dine-in flag. Show-stopper for V2 SaaS.
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.remediation_cost_estimate: ~2 weeks (refactor + sentinel test + tenant resolution layer)
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.owner_action: V2.0 prerequisite — track in V2.0 backlog as BLOCKER_V2_001

top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.title: OutboxRetryFailedCommand + OutboxWebhookRetryFailedCommand hold GLOBAL Cache::lock (one branch starves all)
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.impact: Cross-branch contention on shared cron locks. Tenant A's outbox backlog blocks Tenant B's real-time broadcasts for up to 5 minutes (LOCK_TTL=300s). KDS/POS/OSS sync SLA breaks at scale.
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.remediation_cost_estimate: ~1 day (signature --branch flag + Cache::lock key + cron fan-out)
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.owner_action: V2.0 prerequisite — track as BLOCKER_V2_002, low cost so do early

top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.title: BranchScope drift (10 EXEMPTED_MODELS) + Echo Admin cross-branch authz (V2 cross-tenant disclosure)
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.impact: EXEMPTED_MODELS list includes ZReport, AuditLog, DomainEvent, ActionLog — all reporting/audit surfaces. V2 multi-tenant: a tenant_admin querying these will see cross-tenant data unless scoped. Combined with Echo Admin authz being cross-branch (C6-ARCH-001), V2 multi-tenant has a SECURITY-V2-BLOCKER cluster on cross-tenant info disclosure.
top_3_v2_architectural_concerns.remediation_cost_estimate: ~1 week (10 model BranchScope additions + per-model regression test + Echo authz tightening)
